```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

[ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org) gives one interface to many chat
models. `chat_edge()` returns an ellmer chat object backed by a local
GGUF model, so ellmer's chat, streaming, tool calling and structured
output work offline. `embed_edge()` embeds texts with a local model for
packages such as ragnar.

The code in this vignette is not run when the package is built, because it
needs a model file.

## Setup

You need ellmer, plus callr, plumber and httpuv for the background
server. Any chat model in GGUF format works. Small instruction models
such as Gemma 3 1B or Qwen3 1.7B are a good start on a laptop.

```{r}
library(edgemodelr)
library(ellmer)

model <- "gemma-3-1b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf"
```

`edge_download_model()` or `edge_quick_setup()` can fetch a model first.

## How chat_edge() works

`chat_edge(model_path)` starts `edge_serve()` in a background R process
and connects `ellmer::chat_openai_compatible()` to it. The first call
loads the model, which takes a few seconds. Later calls with the same
model reuse the running server. The server stops when your R session
ends.

The arguments:

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model_path` | | Path of a .gguf file. Give this or `base_url`. |
| `system_prompt` | none | System prompt for the chat. |
| `base_url` | | URL of a server you started yourself. |
| `n_ctx` | 4096 | Context size of a server started here. |
| `n_gpu_layers` | 0 | GPU layers of a server started here. |
| `port` | a free one | Port of a server started here. |
| `params` | none | `ellmer::params()`, such as `temperature`. |
| `echo` | `"none"` | Passed to ellmer. |
| `embeddings` | `FALSE` | Also serve `/v1/embeddings` from a server started here. |

<!-- n_slots -->

## Chat

```{r}
chat <- chat_edge(model, system_prompt = "Answer in one short sentence.")
chat$chat("What is the capital of France?")
#> Paris is the capital of France.

chat$chat("And of Italy?")
#> Rome is the capital of Italy.
```

The chat object keeps the conversation, so the second question is read
with the first. Print it to see the turns and token counts:

```{r}
chat
```

For repeatable answers, set the temperature to 0:

```{r}
chat <- chat_edge(model, params = params(temperature = 0))
```

To use a server that is already running, for example `edge_serve()` in
another process, pass its URL:

```{r}
chat <- chat_edge(base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8080")
```

`chat_edge()` does not send an API key. For a server started with
`api_key`, use `ellmer::chat_openai_compatible()` with `credentials`, as
shown in `vignette("serving", package = "edgemodelr")`.

## Streaming

```{r}
stream <- chat$stream("Name three primary colors.")
coro::loop(for (chunk in stream) cat(chunk))
```

The server sends the chunks together when the answer is finished, so the
text arrives in one burst rather than word by word. The format is the
same as with a hosted model, so code written for streaming still works.

## Tool calling

Define a tool with `ellmer::tool()` and register it on the chat. The model
asks for the tool, ellmer runs your R function and sends the result back,
and the model writes the answer.

```{r}
get_weather <- tool(
  function(city) {
    if (city == "Paris") "18 C and cloudy" else "24 C and sunny"
  },
  name = "get_weather",
  description = "Get the current weather for a city.",
  arguments = list(city = type_string("The city name, such as Paris"))
)

chat <- chat_edge(model, params = params(temperature = 0))
chat$register_tool(get_weather)
chat$chat("What is the weather in Paris right now?")

# The turns show the call and its result
chat$get_turns()
```

Limits of local tool calls:

- Arguments may be strings, numbers, integers, booleans or enums
  (`type_enum()`). Every argument is required.
- The model makes one call per reply. ellmer sends the result back, so a
  model can still make several calls in a row.
- The call is generated under a grammar, so it is always valid JSON that
  names a known tool. Whether the model picks the right tool depends on
  the model. Small models do best with few tools and clear descriptions.

## Structured output

`chat_structured()` returns R data in the shape you describe. The reply is
constrained by a grammar, so it always parses.

```{r}
chat <- chat_edge(model, params = params(temperature = 0))

person <- chat$chat_structured(
  "Maria Lopez is a 34 year old nurse from Valencia.",
  type = type_object(
    name = type_string(),
    age = type_integer(),
    job = type_string(),
    city = type_string()
  )
)
str(person)
#> List of 4
#>  $ name: chr "Maria Lopez"
#>  $ age : int 34
#>  $ job : chr "Nurse"
#>  $ city: chr "Valencia"
```

Use a flat object with string, number, integer, boolean or enum fields.
Nested objects and arrays are not supported.

Without ellmer, `edge_extract()` does the same directly on a loaded model.

## Embeddings with embed_edge()

`embed_edge()` turns texts into vectors with a local embedding model. It
needs no server. The model is loaded the first time and kept for the rest
of the session.

```{r}
embedder <- "Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf"

texts <- c("The cat sat on the mat.", "A kitten slept on the rug.",
           "Interest rates rose again.")
m <- embed_edge(texts, embedder)
dim(m)
#> [1]    3 1024

round(edge_similarity_matrix(m), 2)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,] 1.00 0.70 0.32
#> [2,] 0.70 1.00 0.31
#> [3,] 0.32 0.31 1.00
```

A data frame with a `text` column gets an `embedding` matrix column:

```{r}
df <- embed_edge(data.frame(text = texts), embedder)
dim(df$embedding)
```

Called without texts, `embed_edge()` returns a function. That is what
`ragnar::ragnar_store_create(embed = )` takes. The function refers to the
model by its path only, so a saved store still works in a new session.

```{r}
store <- ragnar::ragnar_store_create(
  "docs.duckdb",
  embed = embed_edge(model_path = embedder)
)
```

Use an embedding model here, not a chat model. A chat model gives weaker
vectors. `chat_edge(embeddings = TRUE)` can serve `/v1/embeddings` from
the chat model, but it slows chat and uses more memory.

For retrieval without ragnar, see
`vignette("rag", package = "edgemodelr")`.
